title: One JD source: a picked role stays linked through edits, files and tab switches

body:
## Summary
The JD column is three independent state atoms (`jobDescriptionFile`, `jobDescriptionText`, `selectedJdSlug`). The rule that binds them (one active source, and a slug only when its body is what gets sent) is enforced by hand at six call sites. Three live defects fall out of that. The role link is dropped on every tab switch. A typo fix silently unlinks the role. Picking a saved JD while a JD file is attached scores the file's prose, grounds it on the picked role's requirements and files it under that role. This card replaces the three atoms with one `JdSource` value behind one patch door.

## Description
`analyzeJdSource.ts` (pure, no React) owns a discriminated union: `none | typed{text} | file{file} | saved{slug, text, baseline, state: loading|ready|failed, edited}`. It has one transition function (`pickSaved`, `bodyLoaded`, `bodyFailed`, `edit`, `revert`, `unlink`, `attachFile`, `removeFile`, `clear`, `restore`) and two projections. `jdSubmission(source)` returns exactly what `executeAnalysis` sends: never file+slug and never file+text. `jdStatus(source, library)` returns the column/collapsed label, which becomes 'Linked to <title>' or 'Edited from <title>' instead of a character count. `useAnalyzeJdLibrary` keeps the fetches, the pick sequence counter and the library state, and dispatches into the source. `useAnalyzeForm` holds one `useState<JdSource>` and derives `hasJobDescription`, `library.selectedJdSlug` (kept as a projection so the hook's public shape, and any card reading it, is unchanged) and `inputs.jobDescriptionText/File`. The draft gains optional `jdSlug` and `jdEdited`. A restored link is re-checked against the library once it has loaded, and it is dropped with a visible 'linkGone' notice only when a complete, non-truncated library proves the role is gone.

One behaviour is decided here and named for the deck. Editing a saved JD's text keeps the role link and marks it edited, with Revert and Unlink one click away. Today it detaches silently. The role's structured requirements still ground the score, which is what the recruiter picked; the edit changes prose, not the requisition. A file attach replaces the pasted text instead of sitting beside it. That text was never sent next to a file anyway (analyze-run.ts:207-208), so the change removes a silent discard; it does not add a loss.

No server change, no new route, no new error code (catalog adds about 5 `analyze.*` labels). There is no read->write against the store, so no lock or re-check applies. The existing pick-sequence counter stays the guard against a slow body fetch landing after a newer pick. Perf: +1 leaf module in the Analyze chunk (app/page.tsx graph via next/dynamic), which is already 1 KB over the ceiling on the working tree, so the coordinator settles perf-budget.json.

## Flow
1. Write `analyzeJdSource.test.ts` first: the 8 acceptance cases plus a transition-sequence property (no reachable state projects file+slug or file+text).
2. Implement `analyzeJdSource.ts` and extend `analyzeDraft.ts` with `jdSlug`/`jdEdited` and `restoreJdSource`; extend `analyzeDraft.test.ts`.
3. Cut `useAnalyzeJdLibrary` and `useAnalyzeForm` over to the single source; keep `library.selectedJdSlug`, `inputs.jobDescriptionText/File` as derived projections.
4. Route the intake router (`useAnalyzeFileAccept`) and the column (`AnalyzeFormOptionalColumns`) through the door; update the `analyzeFileIntakeGate.test.ts` source pin.
5. Picker shows Linked/Edited state with Revert and Unlink; add the catalog keys in all four locales; one paragraph in docs/features/candidates/README.md (the JD-source rule and the draft's role link).

## Expected impact
A recruiter who deep-links from a role into Analyze, checks the pipeline in another tab and comes back gets a run that is still grounded on the role's must/nice requirements and still addable to its lane. Today they silently get a prose-only score and a disabled Add-to-pipeline. The file-plus-pick mis-tag, a candidate filed under a role whose JD they were never scored against, closes as a class because the projection cannot express it. Every later change to the JD column goes through one tested module.

## Evaluation
Claim: one JD source value closes the tab-switch unlink, the silent edit unlink and the file-plus-pick mis-tag, and makes the role link visible.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (analyzeJdSource.ts does not exist; the draft drops the slug; pickJd leaves the file attached).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over analyzeJdSource.test.ts, analyzeDraft.test.ts and analyzeFileIntakeGate.test.ts, then the integration gate (tsc, lint, i18n:check, test:perf, test:unit).
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture

body:
## Summary
The recruiter decides blind whether to spend a run. The app already knows, by the CV's content hash, whether this exact document was scored for this role, what it scored and what was decided. A re-run of a candidate decided 'pass' also quietly resurrects them as undecided in History, because History shows only the newest row per (cv_hash, jd_slug) and a new row carries no disposition. A 'Seen before' strip above the Analyze button shows that footprint before the spend: same role, the latest score and date, the recorded decision with a link to the report that holds it, and the other roles this CV was analyzed for.

## Description
When CVs are attached (and the run is not blind), the strip hashes each file with the same `cvVariantHash` the server persists. It asks a new gated read, `GET /api/analyze/prior?cv=<hash>[&cv=...]&jd=<slug>`, and renders `summarizePriorRuns`: verdict `none | seen-elsewhere | seen | decided`. For `decided` it names the disposition and date, links /history/<slug> ('Open the decided report'), and states the consequence in plain words: a new run is listed in History as undecided, and the decision stays on the earlier report. For `seen` (scored, not decided) it offers the latest report link. Other roles are listed up to 3. The Analyze button stays enabled: this is information, not a gate, so no refusal is added and no other surface needs to learn one. The store read lives in a new slice `app/_lib/db/analyses-prior.ts` (imports `./core`, never the db.ts barrel), so it does not touch `analyses.ts`, which r09 cv-analyze-workspace/A rewrites. It is workspace-scoped and pinned by extending the existing source guard. It is a pure read with no read->write, so no lock or re-check strategy applies. Blind mode follows the technique's redaction boundary: no request and no strip, because a footprint names the person the blind screen hides. A demo session (requireOperator rejects the demo workspace), a 4xx/5xx or a hashing failure all degrade to no strip, never to 'never analyzed'. Auth: not on app/_lib/auth/public-routes.ts, and the route calls requireOperator + requireCapabilityCoded('read'). Rate limit: not an open or paid route, so rate-limit-contract.test.ts is untouched. Errors reuse ANALYSES_LIST_FAILED. New catalog keys are strip copy only (about 7 `analyze.prior*` keys, four locales, no em dashes). Perf: +2 modules in the Analyze chunk, where app/page.tsx is already 1 KB over its ceiling, so the coordinator settles it. Sequencing: the strip reads `state.library.selectedJdSlug`, which this deck's slot A keeps as a projection; no file overlaps slot A.

## Flow
1. `analyzePriorRuns.test.ts` first: query building (blind, empty, cap, malformed hash) and summarizing (decided on an older row, seen, elsewhere, none).
2. `analyses-prior.ts` (`listPriorRunsByCvHashes(hashes, workspaceId, limit)`: slug, candidate_label, jd_slug, score, created_at, disposition, cv_hash, newest first, bound workspace_id) plus the extended tenancy guard.
3. Route + route.test.ts on the throwaway SQLite (unit-db.ts first): tenancy, 401, the characterization case.
4. `AnalyzePriorRunsStrip.tsx`: hash with abort on change, render the verdict through PANEL/NOTICE recipes, dates via useFormatter; mount it in AnalyzeFormFooter above the run row.
5. Catalogs x4, `npm run api:docs`, a paragraph in docs/features/candidates/README.md and a line in docs/architecture/candidate-data-flow.md (only a content hash crosses the wire, no CV bytes).

## Expected impact
A re-screen of a known candidate becomes a visible choice: open the report that already exists, or run again knowing what happens to the recorded decision. That removes a class of orphaned decisions (a 'pass' hidden behind a newer undecided row) and saves the wait, and the unit when the cache misses, on duplicate runs. The recruiter also sees, before scoring, that the same document is in play for two other roles.

## Evaluation
Claim: before a run, Analyze states whether this exact CV was already scored or decided for the selected role, never in blind mode and never across a tenant.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no prior-runs module, route or slice exists).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over analyzePriorRuns.test.ts, app/api/analyze/prior/route.test.ts and analyses-tenancy.test.ts, then the integration gate (tsc, lint, i18n:check, api:check, docs:check, test:perf, test:unit, review:constitution).
Result: pending build.
Gate: none
